questions.stem: A new patient with no other conditions has an average blood pressure of 152/96. What is the best start?

options.text: Two first-line drugs from different groups, ideally in one pill
Lifestyle changes alone for 3 to 6 months

questions.explanation: A is correct: 152/96 is stage 2, so start two first-line drugs from different groups, ideally in one single pill. B is the plan for lower-risk stage 1, not stage 2. C is less than the stage 2 starting plan. D is wrong because beta-blockers are not first-line without another reason.

questions.stem: A patient's average blood pressure is 134/78. Which stage is this?
questions.explanation: C is correct: stage 1 is a top number of 130 to 139, or a bottom number of 80 to 89, and 134 is in that range. A, normal, is below 120/80. B, elevated, is a top number of 120 to 129. D, stage 2, starts at 140 on top or 90 on the bottom.

questions.stem: A patient's average blood pressure is 126/78. Which stage is this?
questions.explanation: B is correct: elevated is a top number of 120 to 129 with a bottom number below 80. A, stage 1, starts at 130 on top or 80 on the bottom. C, normal, is below 120/80. D, stage 2, starts at 140/90.

questions.stem: A patient with diabetes has an average blood pressure of 136/84. What is the best plan?

options.text: Lifestyle changes alone for 3 to 6 months
Two drugs in one pill right away
Start medicine now, plus lifestyle changes

questions.explanation: D is correct: 136/84 is stage 1, and with diabetes, medicine starts now along with lifestyle changes. A is the plan only for stage 1 without heart disease, diabetes, kidney disease, or high risk. B leaves high blood pressure untreated. C is the stage 2 plan.

questions.stem: A patient has stage 1 blood pressure, no heart disease, diabetes, or kidney disease, and a 10-year heart risk of 4% on the PREVENT calculator. What is the best plan?

options.text: Start two drugs in one pill
Try 3 to 6 months of lifestyle changes first

questions.explanation: D is correct: without those conditions and with a risk below 7.5%, try 3 to 6 months of lifestyle changes first. A is the stage 2 plan. C is wrong because beta-blockers are not first-line without another reason. B is wrong because stage 1 still needs lifestyle treatment and follow-up.

questions.stem: Which drugs belong to the four first-line groups for high blood pressure? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, C, D, and E are correct: the four first-line groups are a thiazide-type diuretic like chlorthalidone, a long-acting calcium channel blocker like amlodipine, an angiotensin receptor blocker like losartan, and an ACE inhibitor like lisinopril. B, metoprolol, is a beta-blocker, which is not first-line unless there is another reason, like coronary disease or heart failure.

questions.stem: A patient with diabetes and kidney disease has a high urine albumin level. Blood pressure is 138/86. Which is the best first drug?
questions.explanation: D is correct: with kidney disease and albumin in the urine, an ACE inhibitor or an angiotensin receptor blocker protects the kidneys. A lowers blood pressure but lacks that kidney protection. B is not first-line without another reason. C combines an ACE inhibitor with an angiotensin receptor blocker, which should never be done.

questions.stem: A patient taking losartan for high blood pressure learns she is pregnant. What is the best action?

options.text: Stop losartan and have the prescriber choose a drug that is safe in pregnancy

questions.explanation: A is correct: pregnancy is a hard stop for angiotensin receptor blockers. B continues a drug that can harm the baby. C switches to an ACE inhibitor, which is also not used in pregnancy. D adds aliskiren, which is also not used in pregnancy.

questions.stem: A patient with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction takes metoprolol and needs more blood pressure lowering. Which calcium channel blocker fits best?
questions.explanation: C is correct: amlodipine mostly relaxes arteries and is first-line for blood pressure. A and B slow the heart rate and should be avoided with a beta-blocker and in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. D combines both of those drugs.

questions.stem: Which statements about calcium channel blockers are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Verapamil is a good add-on to metoprolol
Amlodipine is first-line for blood pressure

questions.explanation: B, C, D, and E are correct: amlodipine can cause ankle swelling and is first-line for blood pressure, verapamil causes constipation, and diltiazem slows the heart rate. A is wrong because verapamil and diltiazem should not be combined with a beta-blocker like metoprolol.
